utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Tuesday, the 19th of January, 2010. I would like to greet Mr. Seselj as well as all the representatives of the OTP, as well as everyone helping us in this courtroom. Mr. Seselj, today we were supposed to have a hearing with a protected witness, so I will not give his or her name, but I can always give the number. It was V-026. Over the last three weeks I personally made sure that this witness could appear in order to not find ourselves in a situation where the witness would not be able to appear today. Unfortunately, over the last three weeks we had the court recess, and within the Registry, as well as within the relevant local authorities, some people were not in a position to follow up on this case on a full-time basis, which means that last week when the witness appeared, we did not have yet a clear vision as to whether this witness was in a position to come or not. And I only learned at the end of last week, that is on Thursday or on Friday of last week, that the witness had undergone an operation, and therefore he would not be in a position to appear. This item of information was sent to us just a few days before he was supposed to appear here. We found out that he had an operation, and we were not aware that he was about to have an operation. Given this surgical operation, he cannot travel at the moment, and he will need a couple of weeks in order to recover from this operation and to be in a position to appear. So this witness V-026 will not appear today or tomorrow and possibly not in the coming weeks. So we will make sure that with the witness unit we follow up the situation to see when he will be able to appear. If he cannot come to The Hague, we will have a videolink, and if he can come to The Hague, of course he will appear in this courtroom. So this is a new outcome. As I said, I tried to deal with this and to follow up on this matter, but we only heard this information recently. There's another issue as well which does not allow us to prevent those problems is that the witness unit gets in touch with the witness only once they have received an official notice from the appearance here. And it's only after that, that the witness unit can get in touch with the witness or with his or her family to see whether they can appear. And of course this is regrettable, because I don't see why the witness unit could not call before the official notice and tell them, "Okay, a notice -- an official notice will be handed down to you. And would you be in a position to come?" This could be done on an informal basis, but this process is so cumbersome that we are trying to have a translated version from this notice of appearance and the overall notice before we actually launch any measure with the witness, which is why sometimes we do not have any witness before us. So I wanted to give you this information so that you are not surprised, because I assume that as the Prosecutor, as myself, you probably prepared the appearance of this witness, and we find ourselves in the situation where we do not have any witness. As for next week, there is no problem. As far as we know, another witness will appear. It is VS-029, so we will not have another witness not appearing. And the legal expert will deal with the witness following VS-029. You know that we have to make sure that we plan in advance to make sure that witnesses appear. This is very complicated, and we have to be very particular, but if we do not want to waste any time we have to look at every detail. However, we are not going to waste any time, because we will be able to touch upon administrative issues. Last week we have realised that when we couple administrative issues and appearance of a witness could lead to the following consequence: Namely, that we do not have enough time to hear the witness. Given that this morning we have a few minutes, actually, we have about an hour and a half for administrative issues, and I believe we might just as well deal with those first because next week we will have our priority which will be hearing Witness VS-029, and we will not deal with any administrative issues because the priority will have to be the witness, and the administrative issues should be priority number two. Given that we have time at the moment for administrative issues, we might as well use the time that we have at hand. From a personal point of view I will have two questions to deal with, but I would prefer if you started with administrative issues, Mr. Seselj, so please go ahead with the ones that you wanted to touch upon today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have seven administrative issues to raise, and this time I'll have to expound at greater length about them, and I hope you have the patience to hear me out. So I'm going to tackle these issues one by one if you allow me to do so. First of all, with respect to the witness that was supposed to appear today, gentlemen, Judges, you have been informed and received documentation prepared by the Prosecution and were able to see just how many problems there were concerning this witness. My associates have not had any contact with him for a long time now and they have not endeavoured to do so from the time that you said that neither the Prosecution nor the Defence was allowed to contact the witness. However, from the latest documents and particularly from the statement made by the witness published in the press, and I think you've received a photocopy of that press article, the statement he made to the press, we see that the witness has said that the Prosecution had forced him in an earlier trial to give false testimony and that those preparations lasted for a month and a half. I think that is a very serious allegation, and while the witness is recuperating, I think that the Trial Chamber should appoint amicus curiae who would undertake an investigation and inquiry to establish what this is all about. The witness was exposed to threats from the Prosecution that he would be held responsible if in everything else -- if he failed to repeat what he said in the previous trial in this trial against me to protect the witness. And because of his serious health situation I think that these -- this preparation could have been done earlier on and that the amicus curiae could inform you what this is all about. And I think that this time round you would find somebody who was unbiassed to be the amicus curiae if you accept my proposal. The second point is this: Last time, at the last appearance, I was told --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, first point, you touched upon this issue, and I wanted to touch upon it as well but from another angle. As for this very witness, you talk about a press release that I have not read. The Court Officer will look into this, but I do not have this before me, and I'm not aware of this statement, but we will look into this. You say that given what he said, the Chamber should appoint an amicus curiae. The three Judges are going to look into this request, but I should like to remind you of something that may have failed the attention of those following the trial. Maybe not you but others. Before the trial, you made a request for a contempt of court against Mrs. Carla Del Ponte, as well as against some of her collaborators, and you were saying that the OTP had put pressure on some of the witnesses. This motion or request was dealt with by the Chamber chaired by Judge Robinson with Judge Bonomy and myself. The Chamber chaired by Judge Robinson ruled on your motion. As far as I can remember, I will quote the main tenets. The Robinson Chamber ruled that witnesses named in your motion would be heard by the current Chamber made of myself, Judge Harhoff, and Judge Lattanzi, and this current Chamber will hand down a ruling at the end of the hearing of all those witnesses, which means that de jure the current Chamber is still the one dealing with this issue. And this in turn means, and I'm sure you realise that, that when witnesses appear, I ask them questions about the way their statements were taken, how it happened, did they sign anything, and so on and so forth, and this is always in this spirit that I ask my question, and this is what I will carry on doing, and this is what my colleagues will carry on doing when other witnesses appear. So as for point number one, there is already a reply which is the decision of the Robinson Chamber. This is still relevant, and the current Chamber is still the relevant Chamber for this issue, and this current Chamber is not going to pass this on to any other instance. I believe that this was useful to remind you of this, because that way you are aware that we are still in charge of this matter when dealing with any OTP members that could be involved in this process, and at the end of the trial we will hand down a ruling. So this is for point number one. Now if you want to touch on point two, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. President, it wasn't my intention to challenge those proceedings, and I'm quite sure that you and your colleagues of the Trial Chamber will do the job properly, but I thought that this model could be of assistance in later examination of this witness, but it isn't something that I would insist upon. So as far as I'm concerned, this witness is very important to me. The most important witness for my case, for my defence case, saying that the Prosecution used unacceptable means to instrumentalise the witness, and so I should like to have a very profound in-depth examination and inquiry of this witness, but I have nothing against your interpretation of this whole issue, so you can take it free me that I will not persist in what I have proposed. The second point is additional argumentation with respect to your position taken that in this case we cannot apply the new Rule 92 quinquies. And one of the basic principles, as far as I'm concerned, of criminal law guarantees that not a single rule can be applied retroactively to my detriment. So we cannot apply 92 bis, ter, or quater either. Now, in this particular case we had a situation in which the Prosecution insisted that transcripts be admitted into evidence from other trials because it wasn't satisfied with its examination-in-chief during this particular case. We had an example of that this summer. Next, the Prosecution insisted that the witness statements which it compiled itself be introduced into evidence, and they referred to 92 ter or quater and sometimes to Rule 89. Not even Article 89, which states that every document can be admitted into evidence - I'm giving a free interpretation of that - does not imply that we can admit something that was compiled and is a creation of the Prosecution. When we say documents, when documents are referred to, we mean relevant documents from the relevant time, whether it be a court appearance or proceedings or statements given to certain organs, and so on and so on, but from the relevant material time, and not something that is created by the Prosecution itself endeavouring by this product to confirm and support the indictment which it cannot support in any other manner. And then something new has cropped up. The Prosecution is seeking to have admitted into evidence an interview by a witness who was examined as a suspect. That has never ever happened anywhere. And that's what they're trying to achieve here. It's like this: Every witness whom you -- to whom you say, "You or suspect," is no longer a witness. Everything he says, he says as a suspect or as an accused in some other proceedings in case, and it's an old law that holds true in criminal law that somebody who is a suspect or accused has the right to lie in his own defence. A large number of suspects and people who have been accused of something, maybe more than 50 per cent even, in front of a policeman or an investigating judge or a prosecutor lies by placing the blame on others, and nobody can prosecute him for that. And now we had a case here where a man was interviewed three times by the Prosecution over a long period of time as a suspect, and he fended as well as he could to get out of the situation and pass the blame on to somebody else and to relieve himself of the blame by accusing somebody else. And then the Prosecution says, Now, what you've just told us defending your own position, you're going to say that same thing in another trial in support of the indictment against such and such a person. So those are absolutely impermissible methods. All right if he says these things in the courtroom, but if he doesn't say this in the courtroom then the Prosecution tells him, Well, we're going to ask that the transcript and document of his interview be admitted into evidence. So that is my objection there. Now, the third point, Croatian television, on the 15th of January --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, as for point two, there will be part of an answer because the Prosecutor for last week's witness has asked for its written statement to be admitted, and so the Chamber will rule on this. You have also mentioned the retroactive effects of Rule 92 bis and ter and quinquies as well as quater, stating that there could not be any retractive application. We have already dealt with this issue at length, but for those following the trial, of course, they need to have all information. I'm sure that you know of Rule 6(D) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence saying that modifications will enter into force seven days after their publication so -- but this is without prejudice for the accused. So the question is whether there is any prejudice for the accused, and this has to be looked into. I have not yet identified the case. I understood that the Appeals Chamber has been asked or will be asked to deal with this issue through a pending issue that has been brought before the Appeals Chamber. So I'll wait to see what the Appeals Chamber will say. When we looked into this previously, I said that I had raised this issue during the Plenary meeting, which had led to the adoption of this new rule, and I had asked a very clear question regarding the retractive nature of this rule, this new rule. So this is a concern that we have within the Chamber. And through the ruling that we will hand down regarding last week's witness, this Chamber will either unanimously or through a majority ruling will deal with the issue that you have touched upon. Please move to point three.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Croatian television, on the 15th of January, 2010, in a broadcast called "TV Calendar," evoked reminiscences of Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan. And on that occasion the editor of the programme - so it's not some irresponsible statement - but the editor said that Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan at the end of 1999 conducted negotiations with The Hague Tribunal, and I assume they mean the Prosecution, although it was said that -- Hague Tribunal, about a possible bargain, plea bargaining to lift responsibility from him and put it onto someone else with insinuations that after coming into contact with The Hague Tribunal the Milosevic regime was liquidated. Now, I'd like to propose to the Trial Chamber to demand and request of the Tribunal to give us a detailed report in which they will state whether there was any contact with Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan or not; and if there was, to explain to us what it was all about, what was discussed, what the contacts were about, and to provide us with all the documents about that. This is a very important matter for my case in view of the fact that Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan is stipulated in my indictment as one of the members of the joint criminal enterprise for which I'm being accused. The fourth point is linked to that third issue, and it is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute. On the third point, I'm not -- I don't know anything about a fourth, but first of all, I would like to speak immediately on the third point. It is true that Arkan is in the indictment as a member of a joint criminal enterprise. It is also true that several witnesses, several statements, speak about his role, which was a very important one in committing certain crimes. It's also true that an accused must have a disclosure of any document which has to do with one of the persons who is indicted either under 68 of the rules or under 66, Rule 66 of the rules. So to your knowledge, Mr. Seselj, is there, as Mr. Seselj says, after this broadcast of the Belgrade television, are there documentation of the Prosecution which establish a contact with Arkan with a promise eventually if there is a collaboration of anything, or is it first news as it is for me? Is it the first time you hear about that now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier -- let me now respond to the question by the Presiding Judge. Please have patience, and I will be brief in my response. There were some intimations in the public that something of that nature had occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute. Mr. Seselj, I gave the floor to Mr. Marcussen, who may say something, and after that you will able to respond. Or do you prefer to bring some new element immediately in order to make Mr. Marcussen's answer easier? Right. Mr. Marcussen, please answer, and then Mr. Seselj will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, to me, personally, this is as new information as it is to the Bench, and I, first of all, will note that I do not see the relevance of any of this to the case. The Prosecution has complied with its disclosure obligations and have given the -- have given extensive documentation to the accused under Rule 66(A), under Rule 66(B), and under Rule 68. And the only issue is whether or not the Prosecution have any documentation to be disclosed. Now, the Prosecution is not -- the Prosecution is not going to reveal who it had had contact with in the course of its investigations, and this is not something for the accused to look into. We will undertake -- we have undertaken to comply with our disclosure obligations. We will undertake to look if there's anything that needs to be disclosed in the light of this information, but it is not for the accused to demand the Prosecution to give any accounts of what kind of investigation it does, who it speaks to, or anything like that. So that's our position on this, but as I said, I firmly believe that we have disclosed everything we have to disclose to the accused. Certainly we have done our utmost to comply with that. Your Honours will remember that we have received -- we have disclosed more than 300.000 pages of documents on one occasion to him at his request in hard copy. Of this is in addition to our compliance with all sort of other disclosure obligations we have. So I'm fairly confident that we have given the accused everything he could possibly dream of, and I'm -- can say without equivocation that we have done everything we possibly could to ensure disclosure to the accused of everything he needs. So those are my submissions on this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I'm going to give you the floor, but you, too, in order that you could answer completely to Mr. Marcussen, I wish to quote Article 70(A) of the real -- rules, and I shall read it slowly: "Notwithstanding the rules of Article 66 and 67 above, the reports, memoirs or any other document -- notwithstanding the provisions of Rules 66 and 67, reports, memoranda or other internal documentation prepared by a party, its assistance or representatives in connection with the investigation or preparation of the case are not subject to disclosure or notification under those rules." Therefore you have the floor now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all a remark in passing. The Prosecution has disclosed immense quantities of materials to me, but it is my impression and the impression of my associates that they simply put together everything that they came across, and 90 per cent of the materials are not relevant. It's just ballast. But that's immaterial. In the case of Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan, the rule that you quoted, Mr. President, Rule 70, simply does not apply. That is man who is listed as a participant of the joint criminal enterprise. Secondly, this is a man who is described in the indictment as a person whose men, Arkan's men, as part of the Serb forces committed crimes in the Hrid neighbourhood in Zvornik. That's in my indictment. Killing 20 Muslim civilians. And I am held responsible for that crime. It's not Arkan; it's not his deputy; I am held responsible. And that's why the Prosecution is duty-bound to submit all those documents to me, and I insist on it. The Prosecution does not have the right to cover up any contacts with Arkan if they had any. The Prosecution is duty-bound to inform me about any conversations with any witnesses if anything crops up that might be of interest to me. They regularly provide me with notes from the proofing sessions. These are matter of course conversations, and they supply this material to me. And when we're dealing with big fish of this kind, they don't give me this kind of information. I just don't see the logic of it. Arkan was listed in my indictment for Bijeljina before Bijeljina was deleted from the indictment. In the pre-trial proceedings, and in accordance with the decision of the previous Trial Chamber when evidence is called on the pattern of conduct and the joint criminal enterprise, witnesses are called who saw Arkan's crimes in Bijeljina, and I have to defend myself against those accusations. You have seen how much I'm insisting on the distance between Arkan and myself which was there. I did not investigate Arkan's crimes outside of the scope of Bijeljina and Zvornik because I was not interested in them in the scope of this trial, and you introduced into the record pursuant to Rule 92 quater various statements, including a statement by a JNA colonel. I think that his name is no longer under seal, but I'm not sure so I'm not going to mention his name. He died, at any rate. You admitted into evidence his statement where he testifies about Arkan's crimes in Erdut, Dalj, and other places, the execution by firing squad of some prisoners. I never dealt with it. I am presenting this now to give you a better picture of how my record of my trial is -- contains a lot of information about Arkan, because I'm held responsible for Arkan's crimes here, and why should I accept that? Now let me move on to item number four, which is even more important. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a second. So you have now spoken about the third and fourth question, which in fact is only one question. So if I understand you rightly, you are saying --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] [Previous translation continues] ... dealt with item number four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Well, please finish about the fourth, and then I'll be able to tell you what I think.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, after my cross-examination of the witness that we heard last week, in the Serbian media Arkan's deputy, Borislav Pelevic, spoke to the Serbian media confirming that he was in Zvornik at the relevant time and that he was in Bijeljina. So he took part in the operations there together with Arkan, and he claims that I am trying to shift the blame on Arkan. He claims that I am accusing Arkan of killing 20 Muslims, saying that this is all a heinous lie on my part and that I am, in fact, attacking him, and so on and so forth. I had to put this to you now because I do not have a way to respond to Arkan's deputy in the Serbian press. I did not accused Arkan of anything. I was trying to put distance between myself and Arkan, and Arkan's crimes have been attributed to me. I didn't even know that Arkan killed 20 Muslim civilians in Zvornik before I read it in my indictment. Arkan did not report to me. Can I go on since --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen is doing his early morning callisthenics here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why do you wish to intervene?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I wish to put on record that the accused is using the Court's time to engage in public relations activities. He is making statements which really are directed at the press. He's responding to something that's taking place in the press which has nothing to do with this case, and in my respectful submission that should not be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So, Mr. Seselj, you are now telling us that after last week's hearing the press in your country, in a story, an article, spoke about things which had been said by the number two of Arkan, Borislav Pelevic - I'm not sure how to pronounce it - who allegedly would have confirmed that he was indeed in Bijeljina and in Zvornik, but that yourself question -- implicate Arkan in a way to dodge your own liability. Mr. Marcussen says it's -- it's not to be done. So what did you actually want to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also have something to say. Maybe there is a nexus, but not on the basis of things which may have been published in the press and which shouldn't be discussed in this trial. We can't start discussing everything which is written by journalists everywhere in the world every day, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, Mr. Seselj --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't really bother you about the information from the press related to my name all that often where I faced a situation where I have to just watch everything that is said about me with my hands tied behind my back, and people just write anything that comes to their minds, anything they want to. This is important because it pertains to the trial itself. Let me try to explain to you the nexus, Judge Lattanzi. The nexus is very simple here. Arkan's crimes in Zvornik and Bijeljina have been attributed to me here, while the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party were in Zvornik in April. The only crime against the Muslim civilians is the crime that is -- that was committed by Arkan. There were no other crimes. In the indictment I'm charged with some other crimes in late May and throughout June, but this has nothing to do with me because the Serbian Radical Party volunteers were no longer in Zvornik. This is the only time when my volunteers were in Zvornik, and Arkan's crimes were attributed to me as part of the joint criminal enterprise. Now, Arkan's deputy, Borislav Pelevic, was not prosecuted criminally at all. Why? Because his party was an instrument of Djindjic's regime until the end of 2003. Well, we can see more of the callisthenics on the part of Mr. Marcussen, but I would really like to deal with this because this is a serious matter which has bearing on myself and on this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wouldn't it be better to let him finish what he has to say and then you can reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My point is that there's nothing to reply to. There's not going to be anything said which is going to be replied to. Either the accused can bring his evidence during his defence case on these issues, or he can explain the relevance as he was asked to. He's not. He's now diving into some other conspiracy theory trying to attribute responsibility to other people. The case is very clear. These charges are being laid against the accused in the indictment for a number of reasons. One of them is that they are part of a joint criminal enterprise. He's therefore charged with those crimes. It's very clear to the accused. He's simply engaging in a dialogue that is not intended to inform the Trial Chamber of anything but is part of public debate going on outside the courtroom, and we have wasted enormous amounts of time on these sort of things in the past, and there really is no point to continuing with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, you see no nexus. I personally see one, and I will explain how and why. Before coming to the hearing this morning, I was looking on the site of the Tribunal, last information we could [indiscernible], and I discover that in Sarajevo there is a new indictment by the competent Chamber versus military staff, military personnel, battalion commander who has to do with the Srebrenica case, which means that both in Croatia and in Serbia and in Bosnia-Herzegovina the courts continue to investigate and continue to prosecute the authors of those crimes, whatever their level of responsibility may be, specifying that in The Hague we have accused who were in the highest responsibility posts, but there are others. And therefore the deputy of Mr. Arkan, I don't know what he did or what -- reproach to him, but it may even be that there will be no indictment against him. It may happen that there will be one. Therefore, there's always a nexus. Therefore, we have seen a week ago also that trial took place in Belgrade where accused were sentenced. This judgement is now being translated, and I'm waiting for the translation to see exactly on -- for which reasons these people have been sentenced. What was their -- how they belonged to the Territorial Defence. Were they voluntary? Were they a member of the JNA? I don't know. This judgement will enable me to better understand what happened. Now I'm just discovering that a person who was a deputy of Arkan was in Zvornik, therefore it's interesting. I'm not just going to brush this away because you say there is no nexus. I say there is a nexus because I am a professional Judge specialised in criminal law, and that's the difference. So, Mr. Seselj, would you please finish what you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what Mr. Marcussen says, that I'm shifting the blame to another, it's really heinous. I never have done that. I never tried to shift blame on other people, but I have the right to show that there was a distance between myself and some other people. You cannot ascribe to me any kind of closeness within a joint criminal enterprise with people with whom I was on hostile terms, and actually it was a threat to my life because of that hostility. There were open threats that I would be killed, but I'll leave that aside. What Judge Lattanzi insisted on, the issue of the nexus, Mr. Marcussen did not let me finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, but I have to ask you a question. Do you believe really, honestly, that these matters, these questions which you are asking are administrative matters or questions, and not questions which have to do with the substance of the case? Such aside the question of what is published in the press and which from this point of view poses the problem of whether we should talk about it here. But do you really believe that these are matters which are administrative questions which should be discussed during a hearing which is devoted to administrative matters? I have some problem with this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think it is an administrative issue. This is a Status Conference of sorts, and it is your duty, Judges, to hear of my health status and my mental status, after all. This is not a trial that is conducted out of time and out of space. This trial affects its whole context in realtime, and it is affected in turn by its context, because you cannot eliminate that influence of your context. And let me finish with my effort to prove the nexus where I was interrupted by Mr. Marcussen. Less than two years ago Tomislav Nikolic received Arkan's deputy Borislav Pelevic into the Serbian Radical Party, and the latter assisted him later on in his attempted putsch. And a couple of days ago I learned that in addition to the meeting between Tomislav Nikolic and David Tolbert in Budapest that while the parliamentary Assembly of the council of Europe met in 2007 that Tomislav Nikolic met with Carla Del Ponte, and the eyewitnesses say that they were engaged in a very cordial conversation. This is my information that's been verified, and I am trying to tell you, Judges, that behind the screens espionage, political factors play a role in this trial, how they affect this trial, in a way obstructing it, in fact. I faced the western intellegence services, the Serbian tycoons, and the Serbian mafia. The King of the Serbian tobacco mafia, Sane, who instructed Borislav Pelevic, and I'm trying to show this to you. Arkan's deputy who himself admits that he took part in the fighting in Zvornik and Bijeljina is now trying to blame me of shifting the blame to Arkan, and it says in my indictment, You are charged with what Arkan did. This is an administrative issue. What kind of an issue is it? Perhaps it's not an administrative issue, perhaps you're right, but I had to raise it. I couldn't raise it in the course of our examination of a witness. That is an ideal situation. We don't have a witness. We have enough time for me to share this with you. If you think I didn't have to share this with you, well, that's a different matter. I will not share anything with you in the future, but I felt this need to tell you this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I wish to stay on administrative questions, and I wanted to ask you what is the conclusion of points three and four? Is this a verbal motion which you are making to request the Chamber applying the rules, obliges the Prosecution to disclose to you all the materials or elements which have to do with the negotiations between Arkan and the Prosecutor's office, possibly with Borislav Pelevic, his deputy who met Mrs. Carla Del Ponte, according to you, yourself, or even Mr. Tolbert, is this what you are actually asking for by a verbal motion, in which case that is indeed an administrative question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Mr. President. Your interpretation is correct. I said that the fourth item is connected with the third. The fourth item just provides additional arguments to support my request from item number three, to show how serious this issue is for me. For me, it's very serious. And I think that the Prosecution must provide me with this information, and that they have to give me information finally about the meeting between David Tolbert and Nikolic. They tried to deny it, and later on they just glossed it over. And I -- they also have to give me information about the meeting between Tomislav Nikolic and Carla Del Ponte, if there are any notes about this meeting. It is not mentioned in Carla Del Ponte's book, unfortunately. May I now move on to item number five?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Okay. Point five.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen is in a semireclining position. I wasn't sure whether he was going to get up again or not. Gentlemen, Judges, you've already been informed that the Registry rejected my request to hold a press conference prior to the elections in the municipality of Odzaci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj. I have to interrupt you because I wanted to move this point -- to talk about this point under another angle, and I wanted to tell you straight away what was my point of view so you can develop your own point of view then. A week ago we were seized of your verbal motion in the framework of administrative questions since now you are doing verbal motions, and you don't have a [indiscernible] collaborator who are preparing your motions, therefore, you do so -- you present them verbally, and we have to hearing for administrative matters. A week ago the Chamber told you that you had to follow procedure, which is to say, one, seize the Registrar; two, await his decision; and two [as interpreted], eventually, if it is not in your favour, you can question it with the President. A week ago the Chamber told you that taking into account the dates it was an emergency, an urgent matter, and myself a week ago, on Thursday and Friday, liaising with the Court Officer wanted to know whether the Registrar had made a decision. When I arrived at the crack of dawn at my office, I still wasn't apprised of this decision. When I arrived around 6.00 in my Chambers, I opened my computer, and I discovered with great surprise that the spokesperson of the Tribunal - I have the document here - had indicated that the Registrar had rejected the request, motion, without explaining the reasons, and that the accused was now in a position to see the President. But what I disliked intensely was that the spokeswoman who normally has three different hats - because there are three different organs there, Registry, the Chambers, and the Prosecution, the Prosecutor's office - had told the press who had quoted the Tribunal rejected the request, the Tribunal, and I say the Tribunal rejected nothing. It is the Registrar who rejected a request; not the Tribunal. The Registrar, who is one of the organs of the Tribunal. And now there's a play on words. Therefore, while the spokeswoman should have known that you had this possibility technically speaking to seize eventually the Chamber, and I find extremely unpleasant, number one, not to have been apprised of the content of the decision; and, two, to discover by the spokeswoman that it was the Tribunal who made the decision. There we are. So I wanted this to be put on record because at least -- the least of things by even courtesy, politeness, would be to inform the Chamber of the content of the decision, and to date I still do not know at all what were the reasons why it was rejected. Right. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'll be very brief on that issue. I requested the legal officer, Registrar of this Tribunal to find the decisions of the Registrar at the beginning of 2004 and end of 2003 and to provide it to the members of the Chamber in English and in Serbian to me for me to quote something very briefly, since the Registrar in this decision, which he rejects my request or motion for a press conference, to hold a press conference, and the main argument he puts forward there in favour of his decision is that for seven months I have been -- I was prohibited at the end of 2003 and beginning of 2004 all communication with my family, with my friends, with my associates, banning me from having any visits, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, because of what I said just now, I have just been given the ruling. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here we have it, the decision which was provided to me on the 9th of January, 2004. On page 2, the last two paragraphs. Bearing in mind the fact that the activities in the post-electoral period, that is to say, the elections in Serbian had already been held, my party had a large number of votes, a third of the deputies in the Assembly. So bearing in mind that the post-electoral events will probably lead to the fact that the political party and the supporters of the accused will ask for his further engagement in post-political activities linked to the parliamentary elections in Serbia held on the 28th of December, 2003, and considering that great attention is placed on public information and information about the fact that the accused is in a position whereby he can help the campaign without impediment for the parliamentary elections in Serbia while these were currently underway or post-political activities, in both cases as a consequence undermine the mandates of this International Tribunal to contribute to the repeated establishment and prevents a peace in the former Yugoslavia. So my contacts with the party with respect to a possible formation of the government undermine, as it says here, the establishment of peace in Yugoslavia, and this was signed by David Tolbert, and Tomislav Nikolic met him in Budapest.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note they did not have the text of the decision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As of the 9th of February, the decision is repeated and adds that that bearing in mind that at the parliamentary elections in Serbian - and that's to be found on page 2 - held on the 20th of December, 2003, the party led by the accused won 82 of the 250 seats in the Serbian Assembly, and so and so forth. It goes on to speak about my involvement, and so on and so forth. So you can see the kind of arguments that are set out here and the kind of arguments that are used whereby my basic human rights and civil rights have been denied and placed in jeopardy. They say I must not contact, have any contacts with my party, not to give them any suggestions as to who to negotiate with, and so on and so forth, about a post-electoral coalition government. And now referring to that decision from 2003 and 2004, they are expounding their decision now to prevent me from contacting the public with respect to the local elections in the municipality of Odzaci. So that is the model according to which the Registrar is working, and I have been exposed to that kind of work for seven years now, so you needn't be surprised why I use the words I did when I wrote to the secretary -- to the Registrar using the words I used. No human being can take conduct of this kind those were the issues I wish to raise, and I have two more in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, what I would like to know is whether you have referred this to the President of the Tribunal to challenge the decision of the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no I didn't want to raise the issue because I knew that there was a plot afoot. I tried at the Status Conference to raise these issues on several occasions, and every time Judge Agius interrupted me, shouted at me. So you needn't be surprised why I retaliated the only way I could, with a nice title mentioning his name in one of my books. If you look at the transcript from the Status Conferences, you'll see when I raise an issue, this is it. When I raise the issue of the Registrar's conduct towards me - and the Status Conference is the main place in which I can complain about my conditions in detention - he goes mad, goes quite red in the face, blue in the face, and then attacks me in all manner of ways and then switches off my microphone. So what I respect with this Trial Chamber is you've never switched my microphone off when you don't like what I'm saying. And he goes quite mad, switches off my microphone and seals my lips in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What about point six?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we finished with the examination of the witness last week, I was taken to the -- to prison as usual, and there was a new incident awaiting me there. It was staged to my mind to support the negative decision taken by the Registry. I did not cause the incident. When I entered the prison building, the guard who met me in the prison told me that I had to rub my hands with some chemical that was beside the door, the explanation given that this was a disinfectant of some sort aimed at preventing the new flu from spreading. First of all, I'm not somebody who moved around town, walked around cafes or the streets and then came into the prison. I came from the court building, and I wasn't able to shake hands with anyone here. The guards tie me up at the entrance and untie me when they bring me to the floor here. The Trial Chamber members are five metres away from me so couldn't affect me. The Prosecution which is far more dangerous in that sense is 15 metres away from me. The Registry is quite a distance from me and so is the guard here. I have absolutely no contact with anybody, and now they want me to rub my hands with some chemical substance. I said, Give me a tap and running water and soap, and I'll wash my hands. No, they insisted on this chemical. Now, they have been poisoning me for years here, and they say that my liver has suffered, the doctors say because I'm fat. I'm not fat at all. I can get up and show you. I'm not thin, but I'm certainly not fat, so that can't be a reason. So medicine can't explain why, but I don't want to use any chemicals to rub on my skin. So then they took me to an isolating -- an isolation cell in solitary confinement. They locked me up until the following day at 1.00. Then they unlocked the door. No explanation was given for that either. I assumed that they unlocked the door because my friends learnt about all this, that I had been placed in isolation. How they learnt about it, I don't know. When I rang up my home my wife told me that she had heard that I was placed in a solitary confinement cell, that I was isolated. So that's what they did, they created an incident out of nothing. Who can force me to rub an unknown chemical with my own hands on my own skin, why? I don't want to do that. I have a tap in my cell. I have a shower, and that is enough. And I've been vaccinated against swine flu to boot. I was one of the first to be vaccinated against the flu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, regarding this point, I will tell you the following because it is a topic that I'm very well aware of because I dealt with it. As you are aware, at one point in time in Europe there was an increase in cases of swine flu, and all local health authorities have dealt with this by taking the relevant measures, and within this Tribunal and within the detention unit, the Registrar worked on this issue and worked with local health authorities, and it has been decided to install some devices to wash one's hands because it seems that the virus is transmitted through contact, and so this device is also just outside this Tribunal. Why did they force you to rub your hands and wash your hands? Well, perhaps you can remember what happened last week. My colleague, and I hope that he doesn't have flu, was coughing. We do not know whether amongst us others could have been affect by the virus. But at one point you put on the ELMO a document that was a statement from the ex-JNA colleague. This document was touched by the usher. We also gave to the usher some documents, which means that this document was handled by the Judges, by the usher, and then the document was given back to you, which means that if one of the Judges is infected by the virus and if one of those Judges touches a document and then this document is put before you and you touch it, then the virus can actually move on, hence the need for you to rub your hands with this chemical substance. I do not know the composition of this substance, but this -- the objective is to protect yourself, to protect the security officers, and to protect your fellow inmates and to protect the guards of the detention unit. So this is for protection means. Perhaps we are doing too much, but it's better to be safe than sorry, because in my own country last week 28 people died of swine flu or of the flu virus. So this is the only answer I can give you. As for point number seven, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to say something before point six. You and your Judges, colleagues, are here on a voluntary basis, all members of the Prosecution, too, and the Registrar, too, and members of the guards are here voluntarily. If you wanted to, you could be elsewhere. The only person who is not here voluntarily is me. I am a prisoner here. And what holds true for you in terms of your work responsibility need not be a responsibility for me. They could have tied my feet and hands with chains. They could place me on the floor, shut my mouth up and rub me all over with this chemical substance. It is my elementary right whether I'm going to use a medicament or not. I was vaccinated twice last month the first time against the seasonal flu, and the second time against swine flu. And I inquire myself when the flu vaccinations are going to start every year because I don't need to catch the flu here. It would hamper me in many of my activities. So I inquire about that every year, and I have the flu vaccine every year, and that is sufficient defence from all types of flu, from both types of flu. I don't know what affects this chemical can have. What you put on your skin enters through the skin into the body nobody has given me a reasonable explanation as to what is wrong with my liver. Some factors have been upset. Even doctors from Serbia say it's not alarming but something is happening to my liver, so why would I now expose myself to new chemicals, new chemical substances? It's enough that I am being fed by food that you would not even give to pigs. You should see the kind of food they bring into the prison, and I think even the healthiest person will fall sick after eating the food. Potatoes that are cooked, then packed, then frozen, then defrosted for hundreds of years in the civilised world, defrosted potatoes are not used because nitrates become nitrites during the night and they are poisonous once potatoes are defrosted. I'm not going to do that now. If they take me to a tap and give me a piece of soap, I will be happy to wash my hands. But I refused to use chemicals, and they can keep me in a solitary confinement cell, until time immemorial. Now last time when I handed over the three newly published books of mine, Judge Harhoff asked me to provide them in electronic form, and this was repeated by the Registrar in contact with my case manager. However, I inquired. I called up the legal advisor to Boris Aleksic, and he -- my legal associate, and said that electronic version is with Mr. Krasic and Mr. Jerkovic and that they are willing to disclose it to the Tribunal once it normalises their status as legal advisors and when they can serve me and assist me in The Hague Tribunal. And when they are able to come and see me, they will bring in the electronic version of those three books, and that's all I had to say today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Marcussen, any administrative issues from your point of view?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No additional issues. I thought in light of the second point that the accused made that he supplemented his arguments as to 92 quinquies. If I may just state one brief thing on the record for Your Honours' consideration in that regard. It's the Prosecution's submission that this rule is, to a large extent, is a codification to the existing case law. The existing jurisprudence is somewhat wider and continues to exist in addition to the rule, but the rule, as it exists now, is merely a codification of important parts of the jurisprudence, and therefore the underlying principles will be applicable even if the rule itself does not apply here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Marcussen. Mr. Seselj, from a personal point of view, I would like to touch upon two issues. First point, the books. Last week you gave us books, the content of which I do not know. I have looked at the books, and they have 109, 110, 111. It looks therefore that you have written 111 books of the sort. Secondly, I could see that from an external point of view, they were very well-drafted, that they were very user-friendly, that you have a way of finding the pages very quickly. So everything is well done. Given that those books are in the Cyrillic alphabet, I do not know what is their content. I have seen that sometimes my name or the name of my colleagues do appear, so I drew the conclusion that some decisions that we've handed down are incorporated in this book, but I could not look into this any further. I've looked at the cover page, and you had said to us that it had to do with three of our colleagues. And from then on I've been waiting for the Registry to give us a summary translation of the content of those books. However, I asked myself the following question, and I didn't really talk about this with my colleague because it's really from a personal point of view. As a Judge I see that you are writing books on Judges, and that you may well be able to write a book on myself, on my other two colleagues, and by doing so you put Judges under pressure, whereas in fact a Judge should be in a position to work in a serene manner. A Judge could feel, Oh, well, I may be exposed to having a book published, and there could be some sort of catchy title to that book involving what I'm doing. So this is the problem. And I will not push this reasoning any further, because I do not know what those books are made of, but this could be subject of concern. So this was my first point. Second point, and I will have to go back in time for the following reasons: Last week we witnessed a difficult hearing because at some stage you challenged the witness, and you challenged his or her counsel, and so the Prosecutor raised some objections, and the counsel did as well, and there were harsh words that were exchanged. So what do I have at hand to make sure that we have a peaceful trial as the President of this Chamber, because I'm supposed to police this trial. I only have two means at hand. I have a blue button which I can press to stop you from speaking to the outside world, but not within the courtroom, and when I press on this button I'm sometimes wondering whether it's going work or not. So this is a very basic system, because I cannot stop you from shouting. The second means that I have at hand is to send you out of the courtroom, but there again this is a serious decision, and I have to look into this carefully, and I have to take into account all sorts of factors. The image of international justice, as well as the physical safety of the security officer who will escort you outside of the courtroom or who will expel you out of the courtroom. And I want to make sure that no physical violence will happen. And in order to expel someone from the courtroom you can also use tear gas, but also know the condition of your lungs, and in your specific case this would not be advisable. I also have to take into account the fact that you don't have several officers, security officers around you. Today you only have one. So I will have to take into account all those criteria. In a split second I have to make a decision while you are shouting and the counsel on the other side is shouting. So this is very difficult for me. And this is what I experienced last week, and I do not want to experience this again. And after this brief of going back in time, I would like to then move to a question that has already been ruled upon by the Chamber. In order to avoid this the Prosecutor in its various writings said, you should assign counsel to Mr. Seselj in order to avoid those problems. It is true. That would be the easy way out. It is very easy for a Judge not to have to deal directly with an accused and to only deal with a counsel who is amenable, who is courteous, and everything happens in the best possible case, but this is not the way I conceive justice. I believe that justice should be rendered while the accused is there, and if the accused is in a position to defend himself, he or she should be in a position to take the floor. And this is why I've always been in favour of this solution which is to allow you to defend yourself. This is a right that has been given to you. But with rights you also have obligations, and it is your duty to explain calmly what you want to put across like you did for the seven points, and when you are calm I can be calm, and I can focus on the substance of your points. Otherwise, I have to deal with law and order within the courtroom, which will stop me or prevent me from listening to the substance of your points and the substance of this trial, because these are evidences that are brought by the Prosecutor, and these are the statements and the evidence given by witnesses. Everything else is a waste of time. The fact that we did not assign counsel to you was very difficult as a decision, given that part of the doctrine states that an accused should be assisted by counsel. So this was not an easy decision that was taken, but we did make this decision. And I can compare your situation with other accused. You are the only one to have this sort of behaviour. The late Milosevic was never shouting, was never raising his voice when in the courtroom. Every time Mr. Karadzic appears I'm trying as much as possible to listen to the hearings, and we are dealing with a courteous man. He doesn't raise his voice. And everything happens in the best possible scenario. So could you please try in future to only take the floor when necessary. Last week you took the floor, and it was really spot on. Whereon you reminded us that we have to be careful that in Zvornik the Serb Radical Party did not really have a base because Zvornik is in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you were very right to intervene and to remind us of this point, because a Judge could actually make a mistake by thinking that the HDZ from Croatia had implanted political parties in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and perhaps that the -- perhaps the Serb Radical Party had done the same. So you were very spot on there. But when you take the floor just to say that one should not listen to so-and-so or that the witness is a bogus witness, you really have to avoid this sort of thing, and you should take the floor on the substance of this trial, because this is what is important here. And I really do hope and I beg you to remain calm, not to interrupt whoever is speaking and to speak only when necessary, and then you will see, everyone will listen more carefully to what you have to say. Because when you have all sorts of words, of harsh words exchanged, then this could actually be detrimental to your trial. I did not ask to be put on this trial. We were asked -- or I was asked because there was no further solutions. The Chamber had basically thrown in a towel. So I did accept, even if I have another trial going on at the same time. Last week, Mr. Seselj, I arrived at 6.00 a.m., I started the day at 9.00 a.m. in this courtroom, and I finished at 19.30. So I was here in this building for 12 hours. I did not have time to eat. It is exhausting. And then we have incidents within the courtroom, and this is what I want to avoid in the future. So please listen to what I have to say. It is in your own interest, but also in everyone's interests, even if you challenge the legality of this Tribunal, but you've already said so, this is not surprising for anyone. I remain courteous. I listen to you, and some people may feel that I give you the floor too often, I listen too much to you, but I really want to say the following: Mrs. Carla Del Ponte, talking about tracing criminals in page 593 of her book, when she talks about pressures on witnesses, she says that she talked about this with Mr. Kostunica. Mr. Kostunica had said that as part of the Tolimir case pressures had been put on some witnesses, and Mrs. Carla Del Ponte explained that she was going to listen to this point of view, which means that those -- my two colleagues actually took a step back from my position. This is what she said. But why am I checking on this? Because the decision of the Robinson Chamber has to be effective on our Chamber. And so when you are challenging the Prosecutor on witnesses, I have to deal with that, even if Mrs. Carla Del Ponte doesn't agree with me. So I have a very difficult mission here which has been the subject of a protest from the former Prosecutor, from yourself, coupled with a behaviour in the courtroom. It means that sometimes I really wonder what I'm doing here. If I'm here it is to make sure that international justice is rendered as much as possible and as well as possible, but all the protagonists have to uphold the rules, and they must at least have a courteous behaviour towards each other. So please try to remain courteous, and this is how we will best listen to you. So this is what I wanted to say to you, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something? May I say something in this regard? First of all, I would like to assure you, Mr. President, that whenever you decide to expel me from the courtroom, that there will be no incidents, because I don't want to fight the guards. It's the armed force of the United Nations, and if ten guards are not enough, they'll bring in another 20 or 30. Perhaps at times I might give them the pleasure, yet again, to have to carry me whenever they violate my rights as a prisoner, but you may rest assured that every time you decide to expel me from the courtroom there will be no incidents. You say that I shout from one side of the courtroom and the Prosecution shouts from the other side. I am quite amazed that you have not admonished the Prosecution that you might expel them from the courtroom. If you look at the transcripts and if you do a statistical analysis to see who tried to interrupt whom, you will see that the Prosecution tried to interrupt me much more often than I did them. I also treated the witness very properly. I'm always very careful when I'm dealing with the witnesses. Even if those witnesses are false witnesses, I'm still very nice to them. Let me remind you that the incident occurred because the lawyer who entered the courtroom with the witness acted improperly. And when I started shouting, it was because he intervened improperly in my examination, because the only right of that lawyer was to protect the witness from incriminating himself and nothing else, and he started making political speeches. At one point Madam Lattanzi drew his attention to the fact that I was right and let me remind you of that. I don't see any incidents there apart from the improper conduct on the part of the lawyer. Secondly, well, this is your rhetorical A, B, C. In every courtroom lawyers try to achieve the best possible affect with their speeches. Sometimes you say something in a raised voice, sometimes you lower your voice, but you have to admit that I never use any abusive language in the courtroom, and you never had to stop me without me complying with your request. I always stop when you tell me to. So I really can't see what the point of your remark is. I am always awaiting your decision, and if you decide to impose counsel on me, you know what my response will be. I am not afraid of anything. I cannot be taken by surprise here by anything, and nothing frightens me. Through this trial I have been able to achieve all my goals. Everybody in the world knows that this -- that I'm tried on trumped up charges by the Prosecution. There -- there are no foundations for the charges and for any conviction. As far as I'm concerned, this trial is over. You can do whatever you want. You can expel me from the courtroom. I will never come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't have any intention of expelling you out of the courtroom. What I wanted to say is using the tone you're using today, this is fine. I'm not asking for more. Now, it is time to finish. We will meet next week for the hearing which will take place Tuesday, and I believe that will be in the afternoon, after 1400, quarter past 2.00. So Witness VS-29. So I wish you a pleasant day for the rest of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of January, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.34 a.m.,
